body.statement: If \(\text{oeq:complete-two-pass-facet-stream}\) has a positive solution, its geometric successor table determines a fixed matrix \(T_\star\) and finite initial vector \(c_2\) such that \(c_{L+1}=T_\star c_L\) and \(F_L=\mathbf 1^\top c_L\) for every \(L\ge2\); the initial values satisfy \(F_2=7\), \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\).
body.justification: A geometric transfer law is the falsifiable enumeration consequence of the finite predecessor theorem.
body.gap: Finite hull counts can always be fit by an ad hoc recurrence; the claim requires the recurrence to be derived from the same sound and unique successor types.
body.consumer: Researchers can know catalogue size and generation cost before computing bounds at a chosen ordinal resolution.

obligation.what_is_open: Derive the actual finite successor multiplicities from a proved all-facet type system and certify the numerical initial counts \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\) from self-contained exact facet catalogues.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core contains neither the successor table nor the exact row and ridge certificates needed to prove the three nonbinary counts. An arbitrary recurrence fit to the displayed numbers would not be the claimed geometric transfer theorem.
obligation.attempted: I derived the recurrence algebra conditional on fixed type-labelled successor multiplicities and proved the binary initial value analytically. The presolve's reported finite computations were treated as unverified evidence, as required, rather than as a proof.
obligation.partial_result:
If a positive stream solution supplied fixed successor multiplicities \(m_{st}\), where a facet of predecessor type \(t\) has exactly \(m_{st}\) successors of type \(s\), the inverse predecessor property would give
\[
 c_{L+1,s}=\sum_{t\in\mathsf T}m_{st}c_{L,t}.
\]
Thus \((T_\star)_{st}=m_{st}\) would yield \(c_{L+1}=T_\star c_L\) and \(F_L=\mathbf 1^\top c_L\).  The binary simplex proof above establishes \(F_2=7\).  The asserted values \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\) are not derived from a supplied all-row certificate in the frozen core, so they are not promoted here from computational evidence to a theorem.
